entries.title: C0120 source scope: Gaussian directed ground-state maximum
entries.statement: Chatterjee's arXiv:0810.4221v2, Section 12(3), asks to improve the fluctuation exponent beyond its Section 8 theorem Var(M_n)<=C n/log n. Here M_n is the maximum sum of independent standard Gaussian vertex weights over n-vertex up/right paths in Z_+^2 starting at the origin, with a free endpoint. The source does not state this question for the finite-temperature log partition function in general dimension. Var(M_n)=O(n^(1-epsilon)) for fixed epsilon>0 is a concrete proposed power target, not a verbatim source formulation. Current openness remains unverified.
assumptions: Source scope and proposed power target are distinguished

entries.title: One-site hypercontractive upper envelope for Gaussian path overlap
entries.statement: For the n-vertex Gaussian directed-path model of C0120, let P_n(g) be its almost surely unique maximum path, g^t=e^(-t)g+sqrt(1-e^(-2t))g' with independent standard Gaussian g', Q_n(t)=E|P_n(g) intersect P_n(g^t)|, and q_v=P(v belongs to P_n(g)). Then for t>=0, Q_n(t)<=sum_v q_v^(1+tanh(t/2)). This is an upper bound on overlap, not an equality or a bound on variance by itself.
entries.proof_text: Set f_v(g)=1{v belongs to P_n(g)}. Stationary OU self-adjointness gives E[f_v(g)f_v(g^t)]=||P_(t/2)f_v||_2^2. Gaussian hypercontractivity gives ||P_(t/2)f_v||_2<=||f_v||_(1+e^(-t)). As f_v is an indicator, its squared Lp norm is q_v^(2/p), with 2/p=1+tanh(t/2). Sum over vertices; no independence of the f_v events is needed.
assumptions: OU time t with the stated normalization

entries.title: Logarithmic floor of the one-site overlap certificate
entries.statement: For n>=2 and any nonnegative q_v summing to one on each of the n antidiagonals of the n-vertex up/right path triangle, define B_n(t)=sum_v q_v^(1+tanh(t/2)) and J_n=int_0^infinity e^(-t)B_n(t)dt. Then J_n>=(n-1)/log n, and B_n(n^(-alpha))/n tends to one for each fixed alpha>0. Consequently this direct unweighted one-site hypercontractive upper certificate cannot establish an O(n^(1-epsilon)) variance bound for fixed epsilon>0. The result is no lower bound on actual path overlap or variance.
entries.proof_text: Write a=tanh(t/2). Layer k-1 has k sites and q-mass one, so Jensen gives sum_layer q_v^(1+a)>=k^(-a). Summing gives B_n(t)>=n^(1-a). With u=e^(-t), a=(1-u)/(1+u)<=1-u; hence J_n>=int_0^1 n^u du=(n-1)/log n. At t=n^(-alpha), a<=t/2 and a log n tends to zero, so B_n(t)/n>=e^(-a log n)->1; also B_n(t)<=sum_v q_v=n. Since (n-1)/log n is not O(n^(1-epsilon)), the stated certificate cannot yield such a power upper bound.
assumptions: q_v>=0 and each antidiagonal's q-masses sum to one
claim only about the stated unweighted one-site certificate

entries.title: Rare indicator derivatives can gain in Talagrand's L1-L2 denominator
entries.statement: On the uniform cube {-1,1}^3 with Delta_i f(x)=(f(x)-f(x with coordinate i flipped))/2, set f(x)=x_1 1{x_2=x_3=1}. Then Delta_1 f=x_1 1{x_2=x_3=1}, ||Delta_1 f||_1=1/4 and ||Delta_1 f||_2=1/2, so 1+log(||Delta_1 f||_2/||Delta_1 f||_1)=1+log 2>1. This refutes the blanket explanatory claim that an indicator-like derivative gains nothing; it does not refute Talagrand's inequality.
entries.proof_text: Flipping x_1 changes f from x_1 1_A to -x_1 1_A, so Delta_1 f=x_1 1_A. Under uniform measure P(A)=1/4. Its absolute value is 1 on A and 0 otherwise, yielding L1=1/4 and L2=sqrt(1/4)=1/2. The ratio is two.

relations.rationale: The floor lemma's B_n(t)=sum_v q_v^(1+tanh(t/2)) is exactly the upper certificate in the envelope lemma; its lower bound limits that certificate, not actual Q_n.
Both nodes use the same n-vertex, free-endpoint Gaussian maximum-path model M_n; the overlap node studies a possible bridge to the source's variance question.

Reviewed source-scope card says 'Gaussian free-endpoint maximum M_n'; the existing unverified card says 'Var(log Z_n) ... in general dimension'. Revise or quarantine the old attribution before relying on it.

The new 3-cube card computes a denominator 1+log 2 for a rare indicator-like derivative; the existing card's prose says such a derivative 'gains nothing'. Only that prose is corrected; its theorem inequality remains untouched.
